blocks.heading_context: ## Crate Types and Who Consumes Them
blocks.text:
Rust-to-Rust dependency path:
    crate A --rlib/rmeta--> rustc compiling crate B

Native embedding path:
    Rust crate --staticlib/cdylib + extern "C"--> C ABI host

Executable path:
    Rust crate --bin--> platform loader

blocks.heading_context: ## rmeta: Metadata Is the Rust Dependency Interface
blocks.text:
Dependency crate:
  rustc --emit=metadata --------------> libdep.rmeta
              |                              |
              |                              v
              |                  dependent crate can type-check
              |                  before dependency codegen finishes
              v
  backend codegen still running

blocks.heading_context: ## Rust ABI, C ABI, and Distribution Reality
blocks.text:
Do not publish this as a stable Rust ABI contract:
    libfoo.rlib  or  libfoo.dylib   -> arbitrary future Rust toolchain

Do publish this when you need a binary boundary:
    extern "C" API + cdylib/staticlib -> C/Python/.NET/PInvoke/host program

blocks.heading_context: ## Linking: rustc Delegates to the Platform Toolchain
blocks.text:
+-------------------+      +-------------------+      +-------------------+
| backend object    | ---> | rustc link driver | ---> | platform linker   |
| files + archives  |      | selects args      |      | link.exe/lld/ld   |
+-------------------+      +-------------------+      +-------------------+
          |                         |                          |
          |                         | -L, -l, #[link]          | CRT, libc, SDK libs
          |                         | -C linker, link-arg      | relocations, image
          v                         v                          v
                    final executable / dylib / cdylib

blocks.heading_context: ## Debug Info: DWARF, PDB, and Source Spans
blocks.text: `rust-gdb` and `rust-lldb` are wrappers that load Rust pretty-printers and make Rust names/types less hostile in native debuggers. On MSVC Windows, PDB is not an alien layer; it is the same debug-information universe a .NET/VC++ veteran already knows, except the code is native Rust rather than IL or managed code.
